notes: All 30 assertions pass in BOTH configurations (100% vs 100%) — this eval set cannot discriminate skill value on pass rate. The repo's CLAUDE.md already documents the i18n parity rule, the exact UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 regen command, and the e2e-only-when-web-changed rule that the assertions target.

Efficiency is where the skill differentiates: with_skill was faster on every eval pair (245s vs 365s, 145s vs 226s, 123s vs 166s; 26-36% faster) and cheaper on tokens in every pair (-18%, -18%, -15%).

Root cause of the baseline overhead is visible in the reports: every without_skill run distrusted turbo caching and forced redundant fresh re-runs (eval-1 baseline also botched a 'pnpm test -- --force' invocation before getting it right); with_skill runs walked the ordered gate once and stopped.
Tool calls were lower with the skill in every pair (11 vs 13, 13 vs 16, 27 vs 29).

Both eval-0 runs (with and without skill) hit the same environment failure before e2e: a fresh checkout has no .env, so db:migrate failed until the agent derived one from .env.example. No assertion covers this, and the skill text does not mention it.

Grader flagged assertion wording: 'Ran pnpm test and caught X' conflates command with outcome — both baselines caught the seeded failure via targeted test runs before full pnpm test executed (graded pass on substance).

eval-2's 'did not start the dev DB' is only indirectly verifiable — docker state is machine-global and no per-run docker snapshot exists; the absence of e2e artifacts and .env in the worktree was used as evidence.
Single run per configuration: deltas are consistent in direction across all three evals, but variance per eval is unmeasured — treat magnitudes as indicative, not precise.
